report:
Reviewed the complete owner_binder claim, the sole ordinary implementation association in local_syms/structs.rs, and both associated tests. Baseline: independently compared current structs.rs, semantic_spec.rs, and sage-test-harness/src/lib.rs with historical source arrays joined by newlines; all three match exactly. The supplied historical rationale is specific to binder counts, repeated tuple parameter equality, and the explicitly deferred identity matrix; it is consistent with freshly inspected evidence, not a substitute for that inspection.

The claim requires owner-only parameter minting into one binder, reopening that binder in associated-item/field/body queries, adding only new item parameters, and preserving existing GenericParam and owner Self identities. The struct signature invokes generics.check with its owner then stores those generics in Binder::new. Captured CheckGenerics implementation creates the owner/index-associated parameters once per signature computation. fields obtains self.sig(db).iter_symbols(); captured BinderExt copies the existing generic symbols and captured ribs.add_generic_params installs those same symbols as Resolution::Param, rather than recreating them. This establishes the concrete struct signature-to-field reuse path; it does not establish every owner or cross-revision scenario.

The ordinary trait_and_impl_signatures_share_complete_generic_binders test constructs a trait with Self and T plus a generic tuple impl. Visible assertions check two trait parameters, one impl parameter, eligibility, one trait predicate, two tuple elements and equality of their semantic types. These meaningfully check binder shape and consistent repeated parameter use. They would detect a missing trait Self slot or differing tuple parameter types, but do not establish reopening identities across dependent queries or revisions. Captured fixture helpers create a database, add source files, and invoke the supplied assertion callback on its root module; the assertions are visible in the annotated test itself.

The TODO checking_signature_owner_binder explicitly defers trait, impl, associated-function, field and body identity comparisons across queries and revisions, including separate owner/method scopes. Its prerequisite is building that claim-specific fixture/assertion matrix, including owner Self preservation and new method parameters. This accounts for the unverified universal identity/reopening requirements; its empty body provides no behavioral evidence. Acceptance retains that TODO and does not claim full implementation or test adequacy beyond the demonstrated examples. No N/A entries exist, and no new suspected behavioral defect was established.

Execution: I ran review start/read and exact source comparisons; no behavior tests or broad suites were run by me. Coordinator-reported 321 sage-meta tests and cargo build remain separate reported execution. Extra source dependencies used here were captured with review read. No source changes or additional edits are requested.
